rationale:
Split into two children. The supplied proof (Steps 1–6) rests on two standard facts about an n-plane W ⊆ ℝ^N. Both are independent of the cone geometry and neither is available in the imported library scope.
- (F2), the Hⁿ-measure of closed discs W ∩ B̄(y, ρ), becomes child plane_ball_measure → bf_plane_closedBall_measure_eq: ω := Hⁿ(W ∩ B̄(0,1)) < ∞ and Hⁿ(W ∩ B̄(y,ρ)) = ofReal(ρⁿ)·ω for y ∈ W, ρ ≥ 0.
- Step 3, the Vitali covering theorem for Hⁿ by closed discs of W (including the transport from the subtype W back to ℝ^N), becomes child plane_vitali_cover → bf_plane_vitali_disjoint_cover.

Why these qualify as separate children:
- Both are textbook facts (Simon Ch. 1, 2.9 and 3.10–3.11(2)).
- Each needs its own subtype/isometry transport in Lean.
- Both are reusable for any covering or density argument on n-planes.
- They contain no cones, A₂ or projections, so they restate neither the selected node nor any other DAG node.
- They are independent (depends_on = []) and both are atomic.

The cone-specific steps stay in the parent:
- Step 1: choose a_y ∈ A₂ with P a_y = y.
- Steps 2–3: fineness. Apply bf_plane_vitali_disjoint_cover with:
  - ι := ℝ^N × ℝ × ℝ;
  - t := I = {(y,r,s) : y ∈ P(A₂), 0 < r < δ, 0 < s, ofReal(K(rs)ⁿ) ≤ Hⁿ(A ∩ X(a_y,r,s))};
  - c(y,r,s) := y and ρ(y,r,s) := r·s > 0;
  - S := P(A₂) ⊆ W (Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem).

  The family is fine because s < ε/δ and r < δ give rs ≤ ε.
- Step 4: P(S_i) ⊆ D_i, since |Px − y| = |P(x − a_y)| < s|x − a_y| < sr. Hence the S_i are pairwise disjoint. They are Borel because A is closed and X is open.
- Step 5: using bf_plane_closedBall_measure_eq, Hⁿ(P(A₂)) ≤ Hⁿ(P(A₂) ∖ ⋃D_i) + Σ Hⁿ(D_i) = Σ ofReal((rs)ⁿ)·ω ≤ (ω/K)·Σ Hⁿ(S_i) = (ω/K)·Hⁿ(⋃S_i) ≤ (ω/K)·Hⁿ(A).
- Step 6: since ω < ∞ and Hⁿ(A) < ∞, (ω/K)·Hⁿ(A) → 0 as K → ∞.

The hypothesis 0 < n is never needed; both children hold for every n, including n = 0.

subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure of closed discs in an n-plane (Hⁿ(W ∩ B̄(y, ρ)) = ofReal(ρⁿ)·ω, ω < ∞)
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ and let W be a linear subspace of ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) with dim W = n. Let Hⁿ := μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N), B̄(y, ρ) := {x : |x − y| ≤ ρ} and ω := Hⁿ(W ∩ B̄(0, 1)). Then ω < ∞, and for every y ∈ W and every real ρ ≥ 0, Hⁿ(W ∩ B̄(y, ρ)) = ENNReal.ofReal(ρⁿ) · ω.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (W : Submodule ℝ (Rn N)), finrank ℝ W = n → μHE[n] ((W : Set (Rn N)) ∩ Metric.closedBall 0 1) < ∞ ∧ ∀ y ∈ W, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 ≤ ρ → μHE[n] ((W : Set (Rn N)) ∩ Metric.closedBall y ρ) = ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n) * μHE[n] ((W : Set (Rn N)) ∩ Metric.closedBall 0 1)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is the part of fact (F2) of the parent proof used in steps 5–6 (ω < ∞ and the scaling formula; positivity of ω is not needed), isolated: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 1, Theorem 2.9 (printed p. 11; book/chapter-01.txt lines 445–470: Lⁿ = Hⁿ on ℝⁿ), combined with the invariance of Hausdorff measure under isometries and the scaling of Lebesgue measure under dilations. Mathlib packages these facts as MeasureTheory.isAddHaarMeasure_euclideanHausdorffMeasure (Mathlib/Geometry/Euclidean/Volume/Measure.lean:104: μHE[finrank V] is an additive Haar measure on every finite-dimensional real normed space V with its Borel σ-algebra), Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image (same file, line 131: μHE[d](f '' s) = μHE[d](s) for an isometry f) and Measure.addHaar_closedBall' (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Lebesgue/EqHaar.lean:475: μ(closedBall x r) = ofReal(r^(finrank)) · μ(closedBall 0 1) for an additive Haar measure μ and r ≥ 0).

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^N. Let V be W regarded as a type (the subtype {x // x ∈ W}) with the induced norm, inner product and metric and the induced σ-algebra, which is the Borel σ-algebra of V because ℝ^N carries its Borel σ-algebra (Mathlib Subtype.borelSpace). Let j : V → ℝ^N, j(v) = v, be the inclusion; for z ∈ V and r ∈ ℝ let B̄_V(z, r) := {v ∈ V : dist(v, z) ≤ r}; let μ := μHE[n] computed intrinsically on V; and ω := Hⁿ(W ∩ B̄(0, 1)).

1. Since dim W = n we may replace n by finrank_ℝ V everywhere (in Lean: subst the hypothesis finrank ℝ W = n). V is a finite-dimensional real inner product space, hence a proper metric space: every closed ball B̄_V(z, r) is compact.

2. μ = μHE[finrank V] on V is an additive Haar measure on V (Mathlib isAddHaarMeasure_euclideanHausdorffMeasure; mathematically, Simon 1.2.9 transported to V by a linear isometry ℝⁿ ≅ V). Consequently (a) μ is finite on compact sets, and (b) for every z ∈ V and r ≥ 0, μ(B̄_V(z, r)) = ofReal(rⁿ) · μ(B̄_V(0, 1)) (Mathlib Measure.addHaar_closedBall').

3. For z ∈ V and r ∈ ℝ, W ∩ B̄(j z, r) = j(B̄_V(z, r)). Indeed the metric of V is the restriction of that of ℝ^N: dist(v, z) = |j v − j z| (Subtype.dist_eq). If v ∈ B̄_V(z, r), then j v ∈ W and |j v − j z| ≤ r, so j v ∈ W ∩ B̄(j z, r). Conversely, if x ∈ W ∩ B̄(j z, r), then v := ⟨x, x ∈ W⟩ ∈ V satisfies dist(v, z) = |x − j z| ≤ r and j v = x.

4. j is an isometry (Mathlib isometry_subtype_coe), hence Hⁿ(j(E)) = μHE[n](E) = μ(E) for every E ⊆ V (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). With 3: Hⁿ(W ∩ B̄(j z, r)) = μ(B̄_V(z, r)) for all z ∈ V, r ∈ ℝ. Taking z = 0 (note j 0 = 0) and r = 1 gives ω = μ(B̄_V(0, 1)).

5. Finiteness. B̄_V(0, 1) is compact by 1 and μ is finite on compact sets by 2(a); hence ω = μ(B̄_V(0, 1)) < ∞.

6. Scaling. Let y ∈ W and ρ ≥ 0, and put z := ⟨y, y ∈ W⟩ ∈ V, so that j z = y. By 4, 2(b) and 4 again,
 Hⁿ(W ∩ B̄(y, ρ)) = μ(B̄_V(z, ρ)) = ofReal(ρⁿ) · μ(B̄_V(0, 1)) = ofReal(ρⁿ) · ω.
Together with 5 this proves both conjuncts of the statement: μHE[n] (W ∩ closedBall 0 1) < ∞, and μHE[n] (W ∩ closedBall y ρ) = ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n) * μHE[n] (W ∩ closedBall 0 1) for all y ∈ W and ρ ≥ 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Regard W as the n-dimensional inner product space V (subtype, Borel σ-algebra); with n = finrank V, μHE[n] on V is an additive Haar measure (isAddHaarMeasure_euclideanHausdorffMeasure).
The inclusion V → ℝ^N is an isometry mapping the closed ball B̄_V(z, r) onto W ∩ B̄(z, r), so Hⁿ(W ∩ B̄(z, r)) = μHE[n]_V(B̄_V(z, r)) (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
A Haar measure is finite on the compact ball B̄_V(0, 1) and satisfies μ(B̄_V(z, ρ)) = ofReal(ρⁿ) μ(B̄_V(0, 1)) (Measure.addHaar_closedBall').
Hence ω = μ(B̄_V(0,1)) < ∞ and Hⁿ(W ∩ B̄(y, ρ)) = ofReal(ρⁿ) ω for y ∈ W, ρ ≥ 0.

subproblems.title: Vitali covering for Hⁿ by closed discs in an n-plane
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, let W be a linear subspace of ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) with dim W = n, and Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^N. Let ι be a type, S ⊆ W an arbitrary (not necessarily measurable) set, t ⊆ ι, c : ι → ℝ^N and ρ : ι → ℝ such that c(i) ∈ W and ρ(i) > 0 for every i ∈ t, and suppose the family is fine at S: for every x ∈ S and ε > 0 there is i ∈ t with c(i) = x and ρ(i) ≤ ε. Then there is a countable u ⊆ t such that the sets D_i := W ∩ B̄(c(i), ρ(i)) (i ∈ u) are pairwise disjoint as an indexed family (D_i ∩ D_k = ∅ for distinct i, k ∈ u) and Hⁿ(S ∖ ⋃_{i∈u} D_i) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (W : Submodule ℝ (Rn N)), finrank ℝ W = n → ∀ (ι : Type) (S : Set (Rn N)) (t : Set ι) (c : ι → Rn N) (ρ : ι → ℝ), S ⊆ (W : Set (Rn N)) → (∀ i ∈ t, c i ∈ W ∧ 0 < ρ i) → (∀ x ∈ S, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ i ∈ t, c i = x ∧ ρ i ≤ ε) → ∃ u ⊆ t, u.Countable ∧ u.PairwiseDisjoint (fun i ↦ (W : Set (Rn N)) ∩ Metric.closedBall (c i) (ρ i)) ∧ μHE[n] (S \ ⋃ i ∈ u, ((W : Set (Rn N)) ∩ Metric.closedBall (c i) (ρ i))) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is step 3 of the parent proof, isolated: the Vitali covering theorem for the doubling measure Hⁿ restricted to the n-plane W, i.e. Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 1, Definition 3.10 (Symmetric Vitali Property) and Remark 3.11(2) (printed pp. 17–18; book/chapter-01.txt lines 765–799), where that property is derived for doubling measures on separable spaces from the 5-times covering lemma 3.4 and Corollary 3.5 (lines 609–660). Since Hⁿ restricted to W has infinite total mass when n ≥ 1 (so the finite-mass hypothesis of Simon 3.11(2) is unavailable), and S need be neither measurable nor of finite measure, we use the locally finite form of this theorem in Mathlib, Vitali.exists_disjoint_covering_ae (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Covering/Vitali.lean:237): let α be a second-countable pseudometric space whose σ-algebra contains the open sets, μ a locally finite measure on α, s ⊆ α arbitrary, t ⊆ ι, C ≥ 0, r : ι → ℝ, c : ι → α and B : ι → Set α such that for every a ∈ t: B a ⊆ B̄(c a, r a), μ(B̄(c a, 3 r a)) ≤ C · μ(B a), interior(B a) ≠ ∅ and B a is closed; and for every x ∈ s and ε > 0 there is a ∈ t with r a ≤ ε and c a = x. Then there is a countable u ⊆ t such that (B a)_{a∈u} is pairwise disjoint and μ(s ∖ ⋃_{a∈u} B a) = 0.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^N. V := W regarded as a type (the subtype {x // x ∈ W}) with the induced norm and metric and the induced σ-algebra (= the Borel σ-algebra of V, Mathlib Subtype.borelSpace); j : V → ℝ^N the inclusion; B̄_V(z, r) := {v ∈ V : dist(v, z) ≤ r}; μ := μHE[n] computed intrinsically on V; D_i := W ∩ B̄(c(i), ρ(i)).

1. Properties of V and μ. V is a finite-dimensional real normed space of dimension n, hence a proper (so locally compact) and second-countable metric space whose σ-algebra contains the open sets. Replacing n by finrank_ℝ V (in Lean: subst the hypothesis finrank ℝ W = n), μ = μHE[finrank V] is an additive Haar measure on V (Mathlib isAddHaarMeasure_euclideanHausdorffMeasure), hence finite on compact sets and therefore locally finite; moreover μ(B̄_V(z, r)) = ofReal(rⁿ) · μ(B̄_V(0, 1)) for all z ∈ V and r ≥ 0 (Mathlib Measure.addHaar_closedBall').

2. Lifted data. For i ∈ ι put c′(i) := ⟨c(i), h⟩ ∈ V if h : c(i) ∈ W, and c′(i) := 0 otherwise. By hypothesis c(i) ∈ W for i ∈ t, so j(c′(i)) = c(i) for every i ∈ t. Put B_i := B̄_V(c′(i), ρ(i)) and S′ := j⁻¹(S) ⊆ V.

3. Images of the balls. For i ∈ t, j(B_i) = D_i. Indeed dist(v, c′(i)) = |j v − j c′(i)| = |j v − c(i)| for v ∈ V (Subtype.dist_eq), so v ∈ B_i iff j v ∈ B̄(c(i), ρ(i)), and always j v ∈ W; conversely every x ∈ D_i equals j⟨x, x ∈ W⟩ with ⟨x, x ∈ W⟩ ∈ B_i.

4. Hypotheses of the Vitali theorem on (V, μ), with s := S′, the index set t, radii ρ, centres c′, sets B and constant C := 3ⁿ. Let i ∈ t, so ρ(i) > 0.
 (a) B_i ⊆ B̄_V(c′(i), ρ(i)) (they are equal).
 (b) Doubling: by 1, μ(B̄_V(c′(i), 3ρ(i))) = ofReal((3ρ(i))ⁿ) · μ(B̄_V(0, 1)) = ofReal(3ⁿ) · ofReal(ρ(i)ⁿ) · μ(B̄_V(0, 1)) = 3ⁿ · μ(B_i), using (3ρ)ⁿ = 3ⁿρⁿ, ofReal(ab) = ofReal(a) · ofReal(b) for a, b ≥ 0, and ofReal(3ⁿ) = 3ⁿ; in particular μ(B̄_V(c′(i), 3ρ(i))) ≤ 3ⁿ · μ(B_i).
 (c) The interior of B_i contains the open ball B_V(c′(i), ρ(i)), which contains c′(i) because ρ(i) > 0; so interior(B_i) ≠ ∅.
 (d) B_i is closed (closed balls are closed).
 (e) Fineness on S′: let x ∈ S′, i.e. j x ∈ S, and ε > 0. By the fineness hypothesis there is i ∈ t with c(i) = j x and ρ(i) ≤ ε. Then j(c′(i)) = c(i) = j x, and j is injective, so c′(i) = x.

5. Vitali. By 1 and 4 the Vitali covering theorem (Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_covering_ae; S′ need not be measurable) yields a countable u ⊆ t such that (B_i)_{i∈u} is pairwise disjoint and μ(S′ ∖ ⋃_{i∈u} B_i) = 0.

6. Disjointness of the discs. Let i, k ∈ u with i ≠ k. By 3 (as u ⊆ t), D_i = j(B_i) and D_k = j(B_k). Since j is injective and B_i ∩ B_k = ∅, D_i ∩ D_k = j(B_i ∩ B_k) = ∅. So (D_i)_{i∈u} is pairwise disjoint.

7. The uncovered part. Claim: S ∖ ⋃_{i∈u} D_i = j(S′ ∖ ⋃_{i∈u} B_i). (⊆) Let x ∈ S with x ∉ D_i for every i ∈ u. Since S ⊆ W, x = j x′ with x′ := ⟨x, x ∈ W⟩ ∈ S′. If x′ ∈ B_i for some i ∈ u, then x = j x′ ∈ j(B_i) = D_i by 3, a contradiction; hence x′ ∈ S′ ∖ ⋃_{i∈u} B_i. (⊇) Let x′ ∈ S′ ∖ ⋃_{i∈u} B_i; then j x′ ∈ S. If j x′ ∈ D_i = j(B_i) for some i ∈ u, then j x′ = j b for some b ∈ B_i, so x′ = b ∈ B_i by injectivity of j, a contradiction.

8. Transfer of the null set. j is an isometry (Mathlib isometry_subtype_coe), so Hⁿ(j(E)) = μHE[n](E) = μ(E) for every E ⊆ V (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). By 7 and 5, Hⁿ(S ∖ ⋃_{i∈u} D_i) = μ(S′ ∖ ⋃_{i∈u} B_i) = 0. Together with u ⊆ t, u countable (5) and the pairwise disjointness of (D_i)_{i∈u} (6), u is as required. ∎
proof_key_steps: Work in the subtype V = W: with n = finrank V, μ := μHE[n] on V is an additive Haar measure, hence locally finite, and μ(B̄_V(z, 3r)) = 3ⁿ μ(B̄_V(z, r)) (Measure.addHaar_closedBall').
Lift the centres to c′(i) ∈ V and let B_i := B̄_V(c′(i), ρ(i)); the inclusion j maps B_i onto D_i = W ∩ B̄(c(i), ρ(i)) for i ∈ t.
The B_i are closed with nonempty interior, 3ⁿ-doubling, and fine at S′ := j⁻¹(S); Vitali.exists_disjoint_covering_ae gives a countable u ⊆ t with (B_i)_{i∈u} disjoint and μ(S′ ∖ ⋃_{i∈u} B_i) = 0.
Transfer along the injective isometry j: the D_i (i ∈ u) are pairwise disjoint and S ∖ ⋃ D_i = j(S′ ∖ ⋃ B_i), so Hⁿ(S ∖ ⋃_{i∈u} D_i) = 0.
